These are guides for teaching, not prefilled learner evidence. Use a separate adult model. Accept a suitable alternative with a reason. Record access help and content prompts.

This is my paper plan. No food is used. I choose a pear and a drink of water. Fruit can be part of a healthy snack. I need a plate and a cup. First check food, wash hands and get clean kit. Then get the snack ready with an adult and clear up.
A suitable fruit or vegetable choice with water is one simple option. Plain yoghurt or wholemeal bread may also fit. Suitability depends on individual needs; use paper cards only.
Accept “It is fruit”, “It is a veg snack” or a suitable food-based explanation. Do not require a nutrition fact or every food group in one snack.
Match kit to the food: a plate and cup for fruit and water; bowl and spoon for yoghurt. Extra safe kit is not automatically wrong.

C → A → D → B: adult food check; handwashing and clean kit; get the snack ready with an adult; clear up and wash hands. Today is planning only. For a later snack, staff would arrange safe preparation, including washing fruit or vegetables as needed, and suitable support.
Food suits the person; equipment is suitable; the plan is complete. No private health detail belongs on the pupil sheet.

Show the empty kit box on the adult plan. Ask: “Is the plan ready, or do we need to add the kit?” Expected: add the kit, such as a plate and cup. If unsure, model one kit choice, then recheck with a different food card. Record the prompt; do not count the model as the learner’s own plan.

A food choice alone is not a complete plan: add drink, suitable kit and a check. The cards show the planned snack routine; they do not authorise food preparation today. A suitable snack need not contain every food group. Do not rank learners or families by food choices.

Teacher: Use Support Cards pages 1–2. The four planned snack steps are: check food with an adult; wash hands and get clean kit; get the snack ready with an adult; clear up and wash hands. The learner plans a later snack; they do not prepare it today. Modelled adult work stays separate.
First and then: First choose food and drink. Then list the kit and check the plan.

Aspire: Complete the same plan, then suggest a suitable change if an item is not available. Explain why the new plan still works. No extra food preparation is required.
Evidence: An individual snack plan showing food, drink, a reason, equipment, ordered steps and an adult check; actual response mode, support and a next step are recorded.
